reason: B opens with two fully dramatized scenes — Socrates before the jurors and the Hayes trial at the Old Bailey — that give a general reader people, rooms and consequences to follow before any definition arrives, and it keeps changing archives (Manu, Keeley, Njals saga, Aztec tribute) so each new section brings fresh material. A returns to the same Schoneck-Kilianstadten grave at least six times, restating in slightly different words that bones establish harm but not intent, and its Hobbes section rehearses the same evidence-versus-model contrast three separate times. B does have its own repeated framing about what archives can record, but its concrete detail and forward motion through distinct cases make it both the more engaging read and the tighter one.
